explanations: terra: Some say that they believe while they are not believers, separating an outward declaration from its inward truth.
terra: A disease is in those speakers' hearts and grows because of their lying, identifying the inner content hidden by 2:8's profession.

luna: The section turns the root ح ب ب from love of wealth toward the heart's inner attachment; this ayah contrasts people who love their rivals with believers whose love for God is stronger, showing a contrary object for the heart's love. | terra: Some love rivals as they should love God, whereas believers are stronger in love for God; intensity of love is sorted by its object.
terra: True righteousness includes giving wealth despite loving it, so inner attachment is disclosed and transformed through relinquishment.

luna: This ayah joins attractive public speech to what is in the heart, which is hostile; it directly meets the section's contrast between the chest's hidden contents and outward appearance. | terra: A person's worldly speech pleases and he invokes God over what is in his heart, yet he is the fiercest opponent; polished exterior and inner reality diverge.

luna: Following the person whose words and heart diverge in 2:204, this ayah shows him corrupting the land and destroying crops and offspring, joining the hidden heart to a concrete agricultural consequence. | terra: When that person turns away, he destroys crops and offspring; the action supplies the exposed fruit of the hidden antagonism in 2:204.
terra: People may dislike what is good for them and love what is bad for them while God knows and they do not, separating love's intensity from the beloved object's true value.
terra: God does not take people to account for unintentional oath-speech but does for what their hearts have earned, locating accountable substance inwardly.

luna: The section's dictionary form حَبّة is grain as the kernel of the heart; this ayah makes one grain grow seven ears, each with a hundred grains, turning that kernel into a concrete image of multiplied provision. | terra: A single حبة grows seven ears with a hundred grains each as a figure for expenditure, making a deed's hidden seed disclose its multiplied yield.
terra: Showy charity is like thin soil stripped from smooth rock by rain, leaving nothing gained; removal of the cover reveals the deed's lack of inner substance.
terra: Giving from desire for God's pleasure and inner firmness is likened to a garden yielding abundantly, supplying the inwardly sound counterpart to 2:264's stripped surface.

luna: The section's grain is extracted from husk; this ayah speaks of what God brings from the earth and forbids choosing its bad portion to give away, making quality-selection in produce a concrete moral boundary. | terra: Believers must spend from the good things they earn and from earth's produce rather than deliberately selecting the bad, combining harvest, wealth, and moral sorting.
terra: Secret charity to the poor is better than displaying it, expiates wrongs, and ends with God as خبير of deeds, distinguishing visibility from moral value.
terra: Concealing testimony is called a sin of the heart, and God knows what people do; a suppressed outward truth becomes an inner moral deposit.

luna: The section's “what is in the breasts” becomes an account; this ayah says whatever people disclose or conceal within themselves is reckoned by God, explicitly linking inward contents to judgment. | terra: Whether people disclose or conceal what is within themselves, God calls them to account for it; hidden interior and final reckoning are directly joined.

luna: The section links love of wealth with the grain/kernel sense of ح ب ب and separately uses gold from ore as its extraction image; this ayah places “حُبُّ الشَّهَوَاتِ” beside accumulated gold and silver, concretely joining intense attachment and valued metal. | terra: Love of desires, including heaped gold and silver, is beautified, but these are only the enjoyment of the nearer life.
terra: After 3:14's decorated desires, the question “shall I tell you of better than that?” sets lasting reward against the beloved worldly shell.

luna: The section foregrounds the wording “ما في الصدور”; this ayah says whether people hide or disclose what is in their breasts, God knows it, grounding the image in knowledge of concealed contents. | terra: The commanded warning uses the same ما في صدوركم and says that concealing or disclosing it makes no difference to God's knowledge.

luna: The section describes the final account exposing what was inside; this ayah says each soul will find its good and evil deeds present and wish the evil far away, a concrete disclosure of both sides of the account.

luna: The section depicts strong love of wealth as a kernel in the chest; this ayah says righteousness is not reached until one spends what one loves, turning that attachment toward relinquishment. | terra: People cannot reach righteousness until they spend from what they love, making relinquishment of the beloved thing the test that discloses love's quality.

luna: The section's inside/outside distinction is explicit here: hostility has appeared from mouths, while what breasts conceal is greater, so the inner contents exceed their visible trace. | terra: Hatred has appeared from mouths, but what breasts hide is greater, making the unseen interior exceed the visible disclosure.

luna: The section contrasts inward truth with outward appearance; this ayah contrasts people who greet believers warmly with the rage they show in private and says God knows what breasts contain. | terra: The same people profess belief when they meet believers and bite their fingers in rage when alone; the ayah closes with God's knowledge of breast contents, completing 3:118's hidden hatred.

luna: The section's 3:154 uses the purification verb “لِيُمَحِّصَ” for hearts; this earlier Uhud passage says God purifies the believers, using the same verb for the larger testing process. | terra: God's purpose is to purify the believers and efface the disbelievers; the same refining family developed beside 3:154 is stated as the purpose of trial.

luna: Following 3:141's purification of believers after Uhud, this ayah asks whether people think they will enter the Garden before the strivers and patient are made known, extending the section's trial-and-purification image.

luna: In the Uhud passage that leads to the section's 3:154 example, this ayah distinguishes those who wanted this world from those who wanted the Hereafter, making battle behavior expose the attachment within.

luna: The section quotes the same wording as 100:10, “مَا فِي صُدُورِكُمْ,” and pairs it here with “لِيُمَحِّصَ مَا فِي قُلُوبِكُمْ”: the contents are tested and purified, a direct account of the inward sorting. | terra: The exact vessel ما في صدوركم is tested and what is in the hearts is purified with وليمحص, making the section's laborious inner sorting explicit in the aftermath of Uhud.

luna: After 3:154 describes the Uhud trial of what is in believers' chests, this ayah names those who turned away and says it was because of what they had earned, connecting hidden state to enacted deeds.

luna: The section asks what is in the chest to be brought out; this Uhud ayah contrasts what people say with what is not in their hearts and what they conceal, a specific outer/inner mismatch. | terra: They say with their mouths what is not in their hearts, while God knows best what they conceal; the outer shell and hidden content are explicitly opposed.

luna: The section defines tahsīl as distinguishing what is obtained; this ayah says God will distinguish the foul from the good, naming the moral separation that the grain-and-chaff image makes visible. | terra: God does not leave the believers' mixed company as it is until He distinguishes the bad from the good, directly matching tahsil as discriminating what the mixture contains.
terra: People love to be praised for what they did not do, linking inner love to an outward reputation detached from actual deeds.

luna: The section's sorting reaches even the smallest measure; this ayah says God does not wrong an atom's weight and multiplies a good deed, pairing exact measure with a just distinction of outcomes. | terra: God does not wrong even an atom's weight and multiplies good, grounding the section's minute distinction in exact justice.
terra: On judgment day disbelievers wish the earth could be leveled over them, yet they cannot conceal any statement from God; burial and failed concealment meet.
terra: Hypocrites stand for prayer lazily to be seen by people, so a visible religious act bears a contrary inner motive.
terra: Some say belief with their mouths although their hearts have not believed, and the ayah speaks of hearts God has not willed to purify, joining inner truth to refinement.
terra: The bad and good are not equal even when the bad's abundance impresses, a direct boundary between apparent quantity and sorted quality.

luna: The section's named dictionary form حَبّة is grain and its chest is a collecting vessel; this ayah says God knows even a grain in earth's darkness and that it is in a clear record, joining hidden seed, concealment, and account. | terra: God knows even a grain in the earth's darknesses, and every moist or dry thing is in a clear record; a hidden kernel and exhaustive knowledge meet.

luna: The section's final image is the Lord's khabīr knowledge at the day of reckoning; this ayah names the trumpet's blowing and calls God “الْحَكِيمُ الْخَبِيرُ,” tying that knowledge to resurrection.

luna: The section's dictionary form حَبّة is a grain kernel; this ayah names God as “فَالِقُ الْحَبِّ وَالنَّوَىٰ,” splitting grain and date-stone, a direct physical parallel to opening a shell to reach its core. | terra: God is فالق الحب والنوى, the cleaver of grain and date stone, so the literal kernel is opened and life is drawn from what enclosed it.
luna: The section's grain is what is recovered from plant matter; this ayah describes grain coming out of green growth as “حَبًّا مُتَرَاكِبًا,” a concrete crop image.
luna: The section cites the dictionary opposition of inward face and outward appearance; this ayah explicitly names the outward and inward forms of sin and says those who commit it will be repaid.
terra: Guidance is pictured as an expanded breast and misguidance as a constricted one, using the same inner vessel with opposite capacities.

luna: The section describes the final account as what remains from calculation; this ayah says the weighing on that day is true and distinguishes those whose scales are heavy, making the account's measure explicit. | terra: The true weighing that day makes those with heavy scales successful, treating the final account as measured substance.

luna: After the true weighing in 7:8, this ayah names the light scales and their loss, the contrary result of the final sorting. | terra: Light scales identify those who lost themselves, completing 7:8's boundary at the weighing.
terra: God removes whatever rancor is in their breasts before Paradise, directly staging extraction of a stored inner content from the same vessel as 100:10.

luna: The section distinguishes what is fit to remain from husk; this ayah contrasts good land, whose growth comes forth, with bad land yielding only scant growth, a concrete boundary of good and poor produce.

luna: The section presents extraction as separating kernel from refuse; this ayah says God separates foul from good and piles the foul together, giving the same sorting an explicit moral outcome. | terra: God separates الخبيث from الطيب, heaps the bad together, and consigns it to Hell, a direct eschatological sorting and gathering scene.
terra: God removes the rage of believers' hearts, a present-life instance of an inwardly held condition being taken away.
terra: Family, accumulated wealth, trade, and homes are tested as possible objects loved more than God and His cause, specifying what an inner attachment may contain.
terra: Hoarded gold and silver embody accumulated loved wealth that is withheld rather than spent, preparing the material that the next ayah exposes by fire.
terra: The hoarded metal is heated and made to brand bodies, turning concealed accumulation into an exposed judgment and joining gold, fire, and account.

luna: The section says concealed heart-contents will be brought out; this ayah has hypocrites fear a surah that will tell them what is in their hearts, a specific disclosure of inner contents. | terra: The hypocrites fear a surah will disclose what is in their hearts, and God promises to bring out the very thing they fear will be exposed.
luna: The section's chest image concerns concealed inward matter; this ayah asks whether hypocrites know God knows their secret and private talk, identifying what they try to keep hidden.
terra: Charity is taken from people's wealth to cleanse and purify them, joining the loved possession to an act that refines its holder inwardly.
terra: After deeds are seen, people return to the Knower of unseen and seen, who tells them what they were doing; action, hidden knowledge, and final report converge.
terra: The world's luxuriant vegetation is suddenly made like a harvested field that had not flourished yesterday, an indirect harvest image of outward abundance passing away.

luna: The section cites the particle's weight as the scale's fineness; this ayah says not even an atom's weight or anything smaller or larger escapes the Lord's knowledge and clear record, a repeated formulation of exact accounting. | terra: Not an atom's weight, nor anything smaller or greater, escapes the Lord; all is in a clear record, matching the finest possible sorting.

luna: The section treats the chest as a vessel in which matters stay hidden; this ayah describes people folding their breasts to hide from God, then says He knows what they conceal and declare. | terra: People fold their breasts and cover themselves to hide, yet God knows what they conceal and reveal and knows the very contents of breasts.

luna: The section describes grain separated from its husk; this ayah tells the people to leave what they reap in its ears, a specific case where grain is deliberately kept within its husk for storage. | terra: Joseph instructs people to leave harvested grain in its ears except what they eat; preserving the kernel inside its cover is a concrete inverse of stripping the husk away.

luna: The section's dictionary example is gold extracted from ore and its grain is separated from husk; this ayah explicitly heats material for adornment, then says its foam goes away while what benefits people remains, making the valued core versus waste separation concrete. | terra: Floodwater sheds foam and molten metal sheds dross; the scum vanishes while what benefits people remains, exactly staging ore, residue, and the source's definition of tahsil as isolating what stays.
terra: Those who love worldly life over the Hereafter disclose a preference whose two objects will not have the same permanence.
terra: The deeds of disbelievers are ashes violently scattered by wind, a final account in which no useful remainder can be grasped.
terra: A good word is a good tree whose root is firm, giving the section's inner kernel a stable substance rather than a passing surface.
terra: The firmly rooted tree of 14:24 continually gives its fruit, making hidden rooted quality disclose itself as lasting yield.
terra: A bad word is an uprooted tree with no stability, the contrary result to the source's definition of what remains and becomes fixed.
terra: God makes believers firm with the firm word in worldly life and the Hereafter, extending 14:24's rooted stability into final judgment.
terra: God removes the rancor in their breasts and seats them as brothers, another explicit removal of what had been lodged inwardly.

luna: This ayah depicts a man hiding from people in shame and debating whether to keep a daughter in disgrace or bury her in the ground; it gives a concrete, contrary instance of an inward state hidden as burial.
terra: What people possess runs out while what is with God remains, stating the section's distinction between what passes away and the stable remainder.

luna: The section describes an account's contents being brought to light; this ayah says each person's record will be brought out on the Resurrection Day, open before them. | terra: Each person's record is fastened to them and brought out on Resurrection as an open book, giving the accumulated deed-total an exposed form.

luna: After the personal record is produced in 17:13, this ayah commands, “اقْرَأْ كِتَابَكَ,” and says the person is enough as their own reckoner, completing the accounting scene. | terra: The person reads that opened record and is sufficient as their own reckoner, completing the final-account image of 17:13.
terra: Hearing, sight, and heart will all be questioned, bringing the inward faculty itself into the reckoning.
terra: When truth comes, falsehood vanishes because falsehood is bound to vanish, supplying another exact boundary between what remains and what passes away.

luna: The section's dictionary image separates grain from husk; this ayah depicts rain-grown vegetation becoming dry chaff scattered by wind, supplying the discarded plant matter in that image. | terra: Worldly vegetation becomes dry fragments scattered by winds, supplying the chaff-like passing side of the section's harvest image.

luna: After 18:45's chaff is scattered, this ayah contrasts worldly wealth and children with “الْبَاقِيَاتُ الصَّالِحَاتُ,” the lasting remainder, making the section's lexical sense of what remains explicit. | terra: Wealth and children are worldly adornment, while enduring righteous deeds are better with God, opposing loved goods to what survives the final accounting.
luna: This ayah says the earth is laid bare, everyone is gathered with no one left behind, continuing the section's image of the buried being brought out into a complete reckoning.
luna: After none are left out of the gathering in 18:47, this ayah says all stand before their Lord and are brought as at first creation, completing the exposure and accounting scene.

luna: The section's lexicon calls the last line of an account the revealed remainder; this opened record omits neither small nor large and makes every deed present, a direct image of exhaustive reckoning. | terra: The record omits neither small nor great, and people find all they did present; this is the section's account reduced to its complete final total.

luna: This ayah repeats that abiding good deeds are better in reward and return, a direct parallel to the section's dictionary sense of what remains after other things pass. | terra: Enduring righteous deeds are better in reward and outcome, restating the stable remainder after temporary things recede.
terra: God has comprehended and counted every person exactly, a final enumeration corresponding to the source's completed total.
terra: Each counted person comes to God alone on Resurrection, showing the individually isolated result of 19:94's enumeration.

luna: The section's grave image is a body hidden in earth and later brought out; this ayah says humanity is returned to earth and then brought out from it again. | terra: Human beings are created from earth, returned to it, and brought out from it once more, placing enclosure and final extraction in one ayah.

luna: The section says sorting is fine-grained and cites the weight of a particle; this ayah places just scales and says even a mustard-seed weight is brought, explicitly joining tiny measure and final accounting. | terra: The just scales bring forth even a mustard seed's weight and God suffices as reckoner, joining the section's inner grain to its final, exact account.
luna: The section makes what is hidden in the chest the object of final knowledge; this ayah contrasts public speech with what people conceal and says God knows both.

luna: The section says what is in graves is brought out; this ayah states that God raises those in the graves, a direct formulation of the same resurrection scene. | terra: The certainty of the Hour includes God's raising everyone in the graves, the first extraction in the section's two-stage exposure.

luna: The section contrasts the inner reality with outward appearance; this ayah says sacrificial flesh and blood do not reach God but taqwa does, a precise reversal in which inward quality matters beyond the visible offering.
terra: The ayah says eyes are not blind but the hearts within breasts are, making the visible organ and the inward faculty carry opposite verdicts.
terra: A book speaks truth and no soul is burdened beyond capacity, presenting the record as an exact, non-distorting disclosure.

luna: The section's image makes the final account a careful sorting; this ayah says those whose scales are heavy will succeed, explicitly weighing what each person brought. | terra: Heavy scales mark the successful in the final accounting.

luna: After the heavy scales in 23:102, this ayah gives the opposite result for those whose scales are light, completing the separation of outcomes. | terra: Light scales mark those who lost themselves and remain in Hell, supplying the opposed result of 23:102.

luna: This ayah likewise has tongues, hands, and feet testify to what people did; it repeats the bodily disclosure scene in another judgment passage. | terra: Tongues, hands, and feet testify to what people did, forcing stored deeds into outward evidence.
terra: The unbeliever's deeds are a mirage found empty, but he finds God there to pay his account fully; appearance is stripped and the true reckoning remains.
terra: God turns to the deeds people performed and makes them scattered dust, depicting an apparent store of action that yields no enduring substance.

luna: The section contrasts a hidden inward face with outward appearance; this ayah says the Lord knows what breasts conceal and what people disclose. | terra: God knows both what their breasts conceal and what they announce, exactly articulating the source's interior-versus-appearance distinction.

luna: After 27:74 says the Lord knows what breasts conceal and declare, this ayah adds that nothing hidden in heaven or earth escapes the clear record, completing the section's link between inward contents and the final account.

luna: The section's account asks what remains once other things pass; this ayah contrasts worldly provision and adornment with what is with God as better and more lasting. | terra: Worldly gifts are temporary enjoyment and adornment, while what is with God is better and more lasting.

luna: This repeated formulation says the Lord knows what breasts conceal and what is declared, directly matching the section's inward/outward distinction in another occurrence. | terra: The Lord knows what their breasts conceal and what they announce; this knowledge grounds His choosing and judgment in the ayah's context.
terra: People are not left merely to say that they believe without being tested, so a verbal shell must undergo examination.
terra: Earlier peoples were tested so that the truthful and liars would become known, stating the discriminating result of 29:2's trial.
terra: A person says “we believe” but collapses under human persecution, and the ayah asks whether God best knows what all breasts contain; profession and inner fact are tested together.
terra: God makes known the believers and the hypocrites, stating the discrimination produced by the trial described in 29:10.
terra: God brings the living from the dead, revives earth after death, and says people will likewise be brought out, linking extraction and resurrection.
terra: At one call from God, people come out of the earth, condensing buried containment and sudden extraction into one act.

luna: The section's heart-kernel is a hidden grain inside; this ayah says even a mustard seed concealed in rock, heaven, or earth is brought by God, giving a precise image of the smallest hidden thing being recovered. | terra: A mustard seed hidden in rock, heaven, or earth is brought out by God, who is لطيف خبير; hidden grain, extraction, minuteness, and divine expertise meet in one scene.

luna: The section's khabīr is knowledge of inward affairs; this ayah pairs the return to God and report of deeds with “عَلِيمٌ بِذَاتِ الصُّدُورِ,” joining hidden states to the final account. | terra: Those who disbelieve return to God, are informed of what they did, and face the One who knows the contents of breasts; return, report, and inner knowledge coincide.
terra: The Prophet conceals within himself what God will disclose; although the context is a particular marriage, the same concealed-to-manifest relation is explicit.

luna: In another formulation, this ayah says nothing as small as an atom's weight in heaven or earth is hidden from God or absent from the clear record, extending the section's particle-sized reckoning. | terra: The denied Hour will come, and no atom's weight in heaven or earth, smaller or greater, escapes the Knower of the unseen or its clear record.
terra: Wind, cloud, and revived dead earth become an analogy for resurrection, joining vegetal emergence with bodies brought out after death.
terra: The living and dead are not equal, and the unresponsive are pictured as those in graves; this metaphor reverses the source's image of worldly inner states as buried.
terra: God records what people send ahead and the traces they leave and enumerates everything in a clear register.
terra: God revives dead earth and brings grain out of it for people to eat, joining buried grain, extraction, and revival without explicitly depicting judgment.

luna: The section's opening of graves is matched by this ayah's people hastening from the tombs toward their Lord after the trumpet. | terra: At the trumpet blast people rush from the graves to their Lord, directly staging bodies leaving their buried containers.
luna: After the dead come from the tombs in 36:51, this ayah has them ask who raised them from their resting place, completing the grave-opening scene with recognition of resurrection.
terra: وامتازوا اليوم أيها المجرمون commands the guilty to separate themselves that day, turning judgment into an explicit sorting action.

luna: This ayah says mouths are sealed while hands and feet testify to what people did, a specific way concealed deeds become visible at judgment. | terra: Mouths are sealed while hands speak and feet testify to earnings, so the body's deeper record overrides its controlled exterior speech.
terra: Solomon says إني أحببت حب الخير in the horse scene, an especially close lexical counterpart to 100:8's لحب الخير whose attachment is later sorted.
luna: The section joins knowledge of the chest with the return and account; this ayah says people return to God, are told what they did, and that He knows what is in breasts.

luna: The section's threshing image removes the husk to keep the grain; this ayah shows growth turning yellow and then to debris, the contrary case where the plant's remainder is worthless chaff. | terra: A crop ripens, yellows, and becomes broken debris, showing the visible plant reduced to its final residue as a reminder.
terra: A breast opened to submission and light is opposed to hardened hearts, making the breast's inward capacity and condition decisive.
luna: The section pictures a final account being collected and exposed; this ayah places the record at judgment and says the dispute is settled justly, staging the reckoning.
luna: After the book is placed in 39:69, this ayah says each soul is paid in full for what it did and God knows what they do, completing the account and the knowledge behind it.

luna: The section stages hidden contents being brought out; this ayah describes people standing exposed so nothing about them is hidden from God, carrying the same disclosure into the Day of account. | terra: On the day people emerge fully exposed, nothing about them is hidden from God; bodily appearance and total divine disclosure coincide.

luna: The section contrasts inward knowledge with outward appearance; this ayah pairs what the eyes betray with what breasts hide, showing how the visible surface can differ from the concealed interior. | terra: God knows the furtive glance and وما تخفي الصدور, distinguishing an almost invisible outward act from what the breast conceals.
terra: Hearing, sight, and skins testify against their owners, turning embodied experience into disclosed evidence.
terra: The owners ask their skins why they testified, and the skins name God as the one who made everything speak, clarifying the involuntary disclosure of 41:20.
terra: God effaces falsehood, establishes truth, and knows the contents of breasts; discrimination between what disappears and what is established is tied to inner knowledge.
terra: Worldly provision is temporary enjoyment, whereas what is with God is better and more enduring for believers.
terra: Those who think their secret and private counsel goes unheard are answered that divine messengers are recording it, joining concealment to accumulation in a record.
luna: The section's account brings inner and outer deeds to judgment; this ayah says every community is called to its book on the day of judgment, a concrete record-based reckoning.

luna: After communities are called to their books in 45:28, this ayah says the record speaks truth about them and that their deeds were being written down, specifying how the account preserves what was done. | terra: God's book speaks with truth because every deed was transcribed, making the gathered record itself disclose the exact account.

luna: The section says the heart's kernel is what will be sifted from the chest; this ayah asks whether God will not bring out the grudges in hearts, naming an inward deposit made manifest. | terra: People with diseased hearts are asked whether they suppose God will never bring out their grudges; the concealed inner deposit is explicitly extracted.

luna: The section contrasts hidden inward condition with visible appearance; after 47:29's grudges brought out, this ayah says the Prophet could recognize people by their marks and speech, showing outward signs disclose an interior state. | terra: Following the threat to bring out hidden grudges in 47:29, this ayah says the hypocrites can be known by their marks and tone while God knows their deeds, showing inner content becoming legible outwardly.

luna: Continuing the passage about inner grudges in 47:29, this ayah says people will be tested until those who strive and endure are known and their reports tested, linking trial with what becomes known about them. | terra: God's testing distinguishes strivers and the steadfast and tests أخباركم; this other خ ب ر form makes people's true report emerge through examination.
terra: The deserters say with their tongues what is not in their hearts, while God is خبير بما تعملون; appearance, inner reality, and expert knowledge converge.
terra: God knows what is in the believers' hearts, sends tranquility upon them, and rewards them, grounding an outward pledge in known inner content.
terra: Believers are likened to a crop that sends out shoots, strengthens, thickens, and stands upright, making the quality of the seed visible in developed fruit.

luna: The section defines خبير as knowing an affair's inner reality rather than its appearance; this ayah says honor rests on taqwa rather than tribe and ends with “عَلِيمٌ خَبِيرٌ,” placing God's measure beyond visible lineage.

luna: This ayah contrasts saying “we believe” with faith not yet entering the heart, a direct case of outward claim and inward condition differing as the section's appearance/interior distinction describes. | terra: The Bedouins say they believe, but faith has not entered their hearts; the claimed outer identity is separated from the interior fact.

luna: The section pairs graves with the chest's hidden contents; this ayah says God knows what the earth diminishes from the dead and has a preserving record, joining burial with preserved accounting.

luna: The section names حبّ as grain and the separation of grain from straw; this ayah names “حَبَّ الْحَصِيدِ,” harvested grain, in a scene of rain and crops. | terra: Blessed rain produces gardens and harvest grain, giving the literal kernel and harvest side of the source's threshing image.
terra: After the grain and provision of 50:9-10, revival of dead land is expressly compared to emergence, joining harvest to resurrection.
terra: God created the human and knows what the self whispers, locating divine knowledge at a level more inward than spoken or displayed action.

luna: The section pictures the shell being removed so what is inside can be seen; this ayah says the person's covering is removed and sight becomes sharp, a precise end-time parallel to unveiling. | terra: At judgment the covering is removed and sight becomes sharp, turning final disclosure into a literal stripping away of a veil.

luna: The section's graves open at resurrection; this ayah says the earth splits open over the dead as they hurry out, directly staging emergence from burial. | terra: The earth splits open from around people as they hurry out, a forceful extraction from the enclosing ground.
terra: People must not declare themselves pure, because God knows best who is mindful; self-presentation cannot substitute for known inner quality.

luna: Before the effort is seen and repaid in 53:40–41, this ayah says a person has only what they strove for, specifying what enters that final account. | terra: A human has only what he strives for, defining the substance that can remain in the personal account.

luna: The section says the final account reveals what was produced by labor; this ayah says a person's effort will be seen, a direct parallel to the deed becoming visible. | terra: That striving will be seen, moving the inwardly accumulated effort into outward disclosure.

luna: After 53:40 says effort will be seen, this ayah says it will then be repaid in full, completing the section's image of a final account. | terra: The striving is then repaid with the fullest recompense, completing the displayed account of 53:40.

luna: The section's graves are opened; this ayah depicts people coming out of the graves like scattered locusts, a direct image of the resurrection's dispersal. | terra: People emerge from the graves like scattered locusts, making the buried multitude visible and separated across the scene.
terra: Everything people did is preserved in the records, supplying the gathered material for the final reckoning.
terra: Every small and great thing is inscribed, specifying the exhaustive resolution of the record in 54:52.

luna: The section's dictionary entry links حبّ to grain and notes husk and fragrant seeds; this ayah names “الْحَبُّ ذُو الْعَصْفِ وَالرَّيْحَانُ,” putting grain, its husk, and fragrant growth in one agricultural scene. | terra: الحب ذو العصف places grain together with its leafy husk or straw, the concrete kernel-and-cover scene used by the source's dictionary explanation.
luna: The section's dictionary gloss says the remainder stays firm after the rest goes; this ayah says everyone on earth passes away, establishing what does not last.
luna: Following 55:26's passing away, this ayah says the face of the Lord remains, a direct formulation of what stays after everything else goes.

luna: The section's kernel-and-chaff image depends on cultivated grain; this ayah asks what people sow, establishing the seed whose growth and fate are considered in its neighboring verses. | terra: The question about what people sow establishes the grain under examination and asks them to look beneath their assumed control of the harvest.

luna: After the sowing question in 56:63, this ayah asks whether people make the crop grow or God, connecting grain's yield to provision beyond human control. | terra: The next question distinguishes human sowing from God's causing growth, separating the visible act from the agency that produces its substance.

luna: Following the crop-growth question, this ayah says God could make the crop dry debris; it gives the discarded, vanishing plant side of the section's grain-versus-chaff separation. | terra: God could make the crop shattered debris, leaving cultivators bewildered; the valued grain can end as the useless residue imagined by the threshing scene.
terra: A wall with an inner side of mercy and outer side of punishment separates hypocrites from believers on the final day, giving judgment a literal partition.

terra: The hypocrites admit they once stood with the believers but inwardly tempted themselves, waited, doubted, and followed false hopes; the separation of 57:13 exposes a long-accumulated interior history.
terra: Believers are warned against hearts hardening as a long period passes, specifically supporting the source's picture of an interior altered by what accumulates over years.
terra: God revives the earth after its death, offering a visible reversal immediately after 57:16's warning about hardened hearts.

luna: The section distinguishes the lasting kernel from what is discarded; this ayah follows vegetation from growth to yellowing and chaff, then calls worldly life deceptive provision, a specific reversal in which the whole crop passes away. | terra: Worldly life is a crop that impresses, then yellows and becomes debris, concretely staging transient outer flourishing and its remainder.

luna: This ayah says God will resurrect people, inform them of their deeds, and that He counted what they forgot; it directly matches the section's account that remains complete even when its contents are no longer remembered. | terra: God raises everyone and informs them of their deeds: He has counted them although they forgot them, an exact picture of a complete accumulated total.
terra: God is present to every secret counsel and will inform its participants of it on Resurrection, so concealed exchanges become items in the final report.
terra: The Helpers prefer others even amid their own need, and success belongs to those protected from inner greed, showing beloved goods sorted by generosity.
terra: Opponents appear united, but their hearts are divided, a concise reversal between collected outward form and separated inner reality.

luna: The section's last word is خبير, one who knows an affair's inward reality; this ayah asks each soul to inspect what it sent ahead for tomorrow and says God is “خَبِيرٌ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ,” joining forethought, deed, and knowledge. | terra: Each soul must inspect what it has sent ahead for tomorrow, and God is خبير بما تعملون; self-audit and the divine Expert meet.
terra: Secret affection toward enemies is set against God's knowledge of what is hidden and declared, directly placing concealed love under divine scrutiny.
terra: Believers are asked why they say what they do not do, isolating the gap between verbal exterior and actual substance.
terra: Saying what one does not do is gravely hateful to God, giving the mismatch named in 61:2 its moral judgment.
luna: The section stages resurrection followed by disclosure of deeds; this ayah says death will meet those who flee it, then they return to the Knower of unseen and seen and are told what they did.
terra: The hypocrites voice a formally true testimony, yet God testifies that they are liars, distinguishing the statement's surface from the speakers' real stance.
terra: Their bodies and speech impress outwardly, but they are likened to propped timbers; the striking manzar contains a contrary makhbar.

luna: The section says chests contain matters that will be exposed; this ayah says God knows what people hide and disclose and is “عَلِيمٌ بِذَاتِ الصُّدُورِ,” directly naming knowledge of their inner contents. | terra: God knows what people conceal and reveal and is عليم بذات الصدور, placing outer disclosure and the interior vessel in the same assertion.
terra: The command to spend is paired with success for those protected from the greed of their own souls, locating the obstacle to giving inside.
terra: A confidential statement is disclosed, God informs the Prophet of it, and the exchange ends with العليم الخبير; hidden content is made known by the Expert.

luna: The section's chest is a hidden store; this ayah contrasts speaking secretly and aloud, then says God knows what is within breasts, directly connecting concealment with divine knowledge. | terra: Concealed and public speech are set side by side because God knows بذات الصدور, directly linking disclosure, concealment, and the breast's contents.

luna: The section identifies خبير as knowledge of an affair's inward parts; following 67:13's hidden breasts, this ayah asks whether the Creator knows and calls Him “الْخَبِيرُ,” making that inward knowledge explicit. | terra: Following 67:13's concealed speech and breasts, the Creator's knowledge is grounded in الخبير; this ayah supplies the same expert knower who underwrites 100:11.

luna: The section's sorting uncovers what was in the chest; this ayah says people will be presented on that day with no hidden thing among them, a direct boundary of complete exposure. | terra: On the day people are presented, لا تخفى منكم خافية: no hidden thing remains hidden, stating the result of the section's inner exposure.
terra: Receiving the record in the left hand exposes the condemned person's negative final account after the universal presentation of 69:18.
terra: The condemned person says his wealth did not avail him, stripping the intensely loved possession of substance at the moment the record is opened.
luna: The section says a bird's crop is a collecting pouch because it gathers food; this ayah describes a person who gathered and hoarded, a concrete human counterpart to the chest as a store.

luna: In the same passage as the section's gathering-and-hoarding parallel at 70:18, this ayah says that when good reaches a person, he withholds it, specifying the possessive impulse behind intense love of wealth.

luna: The section stages those in graves being brought out; this ayah says people will emerge quickly from the graves, an explicit parallel scene. | terra: People come rapidly out of the graves as though racing to a marker, another direct enactment of the section's first uncovering.
terra: God causes human beings to grow from the earth like vegetation, fusing the grain image with bodily origin.
terra: God returns people to the earth and will bring them out again, completing 71:17's plant-like origin with burial and extraction.
luna: This ayah says every soul is held in pledge for what it earned, a direct account of the deeds collected within and brought to judgment.

luna: This ayah answers the denial of resurrection by saying God can gather a person's bones, a specific bodily gathering parallel to the section's opened graves. | terra: The human doubts that God will gather his bones, posing the bodily gathering that precedes inner accounting.

luna: After promising to gather the bones in 75:3, this ayah says God can even proportion the fingertips, extending the resurrection image to minute detail. | terra: God can restore even the fingertips, making the bodily gathering in 75:3 exact down to fine detail.

luna: The section describes a final tally of what remains from deeds; this ayah says a person will be told what they sent ahead and left behind, an explicit accounting of the inwardly accumulated record. | terra: The human is informed that day of what was sent ahead and left behind, a final summation that loses no remainder.

luna: The section says what is inside is ultimately brought out; this ayah says a person is a witness against themself, so inner truth remains visible even if excuses are offered. | terra: The human self is a witness against itself, so the decisive account comes from within rather than from cultivated appearance.

luna: Following the self-witness in 75:14, this ayah says excuses do not conceal the truth, a direct limit on hiding what the account has exposed. | terra: Even offered excuses cannot cover the self-witness of 75:14, defining the limit of an outward shell once the interior testifies.
terra: People love the immediate life, naming the inner attachment on one side of the final disclosure.
terra: They leave the Hereafter aside, completing the opposed preference stated by 75:20.

luna: The section links the root ح ب ب in love with the kernel stored in the heart; this ayah has the righteous give food “عَلَىٰ حُبِّهِ.” That phrase can mean despite loving it or for love of God, so either reading turns a valued thing toward giving rather than hoarding.
terra: People love the immediate and leave behind a heavy day, directly opposing present attachment to the coming day of account.
luna: The section's dictionary form حَبّ is grain; this ayah says rain brings forth grain and vegetation, another direct crop scene for the word's seed sense.
terra: Everything has been enumerated in a book, a compact formulation of the completed account the source associates with tahsil.
terra: People incredulously ask whether they will be returned to their former state, setting up the bodily emergence completed in 79:13-14.
terra: Their reference to decayed bones specifies the buried bodily material whose restoration they deny.
terra: A single blast initiates the sudden transition from burial to exposure.
terra: After the blast, people are upon the open surface, completing 79:13's compressed emergence scene.

luna: This ayah gives the burial side of the section's buried-then-raised sequence: God causes a person to die and be buried, the concealed state that 100:9 reverses. | terra: God causes the human being to die and be placed in a grave, establishing the bodily enclosure whose later opening the section parallels with the breast.
terra: Then, when God wills, He raises that buried human, completing 80:21's enclosure-and-extraction sequence.
terra: God splits the earth open, beginning the emergence of food from its enclosing ground.

luna: The section identifies the dictionary form حَبّ as grain; this ayah names grain among the produce brought out of the earth, placing the word in a concrete provision scene. | terra: Grain is then grown in the split earth, completing 80:26's opening-and-kernel scene.
luna: The section links what is buried to what will be brought out for judgment; this ayah places the buried-alive girl before that judgment, turning a concealed burial into an exposed case.
luna: After the buried girl is brought into view in 81:8, this ayah asks what crime she was killed for, making the disclosure a reckoning of what had been hidden.
luna: The section's final account lays open what was hidden; this ayah says the written sheets are unfolded, giving the record itself an image of disclosure.

luna: After the records are unfolded in 81:10, this ayah says each soul knows what it brought, stating the result of the disclosure in the person's own account. | terra: After the cosmic coverings are removed, each soul knows what it has brought, giving disclosure its personal moral result.

luna: The section's graves are opened and their contents scattered; this ayah repeats that exact grave-opening scene in “بُعْثِرَتِ الْقُبُورُ,” directly staging what had been buried coming out. | terra: وإذا القبور بعثرت repeats both the graves and the very scattering verb of 100:9, supplying the bodily unearthing that precedes the breast's sorting.

luna: After the graves are scattered in 82:4, this ayah says each soul learns what it sent ahead and left behind; that is the account disclosed after the buried contents emerge. | terra: When the graves are scattered in 82:4, each soul knows what it sent ahead and left behind; bodily unearthing immediately yields the moral total.
terra: Guardians remain over people, introducing the collection of deeds later known when graves are overturned.
terra: The guardians are noble recorders, specifying how the accumulated account of 82:10 is preserved.
terra: Those recorders know what people do, completing the record that 82:5 says each soul will finally know.

luna: The section treats the chest as a vessel that accumulates what a person takes in; this ayah says deeds have left a rust upon hearts, a specific image of the inward store being marked by accumulated action. | terra: What people repeatedly earn forms a rust over their hearts, giving a concrete picture of years of acts accumulating upon the inner core.

luna: The section treats the chest as a container whose contents are extracted; this ayah says the earth throws out what is within it and empties itself, a close nonhuman parallel to disclosure from a container. | terra: The earth casts out what is inside it and becomes empty, staging extraction of buried contents rather than a merely verbal disclosure.
luna: After the earth casts out what is within in 84:4, this ayah says it listens to its Lord and is bound to do so, giving the disclosure scene its commanded cause.

luna: The section describes extraction as labor carried through to a final result; this ayah addresses the person as striving toward the Lord and meeting Him, giving that work-and-arrival structure an explicit parallel.
luna: The section's final disclosure exposes what has been gathered within; this ayah gives the one who receives the record in the right hand a concrete form of the revealed account.
luna: After receiving the record in 84:7, this ayah says the person will have an easy reckoning, directly joining the record to the account.
luna: The section says no inward remainder escapes the final account; this ayah gives the contrary case of the person who receives the record behind the back.

luna: The section describes chest contents being extracted; this ayah names the Day “تُبْلَى السَّرَائِرُ,” when hidden matters are tested, closely matching the disclosure and examination. | terra: يوم تبلى السرائر names the day when concealed inner things are tested, a concise parallel to the exposure and examination of what breasts contain.

luna: The section's grain image begins in cultivated growth; this ayah says God brings forth pasture, the living growth that the next ayah shows becoming chaff. | terra: God brings out pasture, beginning a vegetal scene whose final residue appears in the next ayah.

luna: After pasture is brought forth in 87:4, this ayah says it becomes dark chaff, a specific image of the plant residue that contrasts with the kernel retained in the section. | terra: The pasture becomes dark stubble, showing flourishing growth reduced to what remains after its useful life passes.
terra: Prosperity belongs to one who purifies himself, a compact parallel to inner refining before the following choice between present and enduring life.
terra: People prefer the nearer life, identifying the preference that sits inside the breast before it is exposed.

luna: The section's dictionary sense of what remains is stated here as the Hereafter being “خَيْرٌ وَأَبْقَىٰ,” the lasting counterpart to what is loved and gathered in worldly life. | terra: The Hereafter is better and more enduring, supplying the lasting side of the choice named in 87:16.
terra: Greedily consuming inheritance supplies the concrete action that culminates in the immense love of wealth named in 89:20.

luna: The section juxtaposes the root ح ب ب in love with its dictionary form حَبّة for grain; this ayah intensifies the love of wealth with “حُبًّا جَمًّا,” reinforcing the passion half of the kernel-in-the-heart image. | terra: وتحبون المال حبا جما names an immense love of wealth, the attachment that the section locates as the grain deep within the breast.
terra: Immediately after the denunciation of immense love of wealth, the earth is pounded repeatedly, joining a threshing-like reduction of the ground to judgment's arrival.
terra: At judgment the person wishes he had sent something ahead for his true life, recognizing too late which part of worldly action would remain.
terra: The oath by the soul and the One who fashioned it establishes the inner object purified or buried in 91:9-10.
terra: The soul is shown both its depravity and its piety, identifying the opposed inner contents on which purification and failure operate.

luna: The section describes an inner core being sifted and purified; this ayah says success belongs to the one who purifies the soul, a specific moral counterpart to extraction. | terra: Success belongs to the one who purifies the soul, a direct inward counterpart to the section's careful separation and refining.

luna: The section's buried inner contents are brought out for judgment; this next ayah says the soul is lost when it is “دَسَّاهَا,” buried or obscured, the contrary outcome to purification in 91:9. | terra: Failure belongs to the one who buries or corrupts the soul, the inverse of 91:9's purification and of the section's eventual extraction of what was inwardly buried.
terra: A person's wealth does not avail when he falls, stripping accumulated goods of the permanence their lover assigns them.
terra: The question about God expanding the Prophet's breast uses the inner vessel as something opened and made capacious, a secondary spatial sense relevant to what it can contain.

luna: The section links the grave to what stays buried until the appointed opening; this ayah says the earth casts out its burdens, directly staging concealed contents emerging from the ground. | terra: The earth brings out its burdens, a close bodily counterpart to emptied graves before hidden inner deeds are displayed.

luna: The section's grave image is a covered state that later opens; this ayah says the earth will report its news, making the ground itself disclose what it has held. | terra: The earth tells أخبارها after discharging its burdens, using another خ ب ر form for the report that exposed creation itself gives.
luna: After the earth reports its news in 99:4, this ayah says its Lord has inspired it to do so; it supplies the cause of that disclosure in the passage about earth's hidden contents.

luna: After the earth expels its burdens in 99:2 and reports its news in 99:4, this ayah says people come out in separate groups to see their deeds; it is the immediate human counterpart to the section's opening of graves and disclosure of what was inside. | terra: People depart in separate groups so that their deeds may be shown to them, setting the sorting and display completed by 99:7-8.

luna: The section invokes this ayah for the fineness of the sorting: even the weight of a particle of good is seen, so no small remainder escapes. | terra: A mustard-small measure of good is seen, the explicit fine grain of the section's exact moral separation.

luna: The section cites 99:7 for the smallest good deed; this adjacent ayah applies the same particle-weight to evil, completing the two-sided account and showing that the sorting does not spare the bad. | terra: A mustard-small measure of evil is likewise seen, completing 99:7's two-sided and exhaustive sorting.

luna: The section describes the account as a final collected remainder; this ayah weighs deeds and names the one whose scales are heavy, directly staging that measure. | terra: The one whose scales are heavy enters the favorable side of the final separation.

luna: After the heavy scales in 101:6, this ayah gives the successful person's outcome, completing the favorable side of the measured account. | terra: A contented life is the outcome of the heavy scales in 101:6, stating what that measured remainder yields.

luna: The section's extraction separates what remains good from refuse; this ayah gives the opposite case of light scales. | terra: The one whose scales are light occupies the opposite side of the same exact weighing.

luna: After the light scales in 101:8, this ayah names the person's destination, completing the contrary outcome of the account. | terra: The abyss is the outcome of the light scales in 101:8, completing the judgment's two-way separation.

luna: The section sets intense love of wealth beside its grain/kernel wordplay; this ayah names rivalry in piling up more, a concrete enactment of that attachment. | terra: Competition for increase distracts people, opening a sequence in which accumulation lasts only until the graves and eventual questioning.

luna: This ayah says the piling up continues until people visit the graves, directly meeting the section's two images of wealth attachment and graves opened at resurrection. | terra: حتى زرتم المقابر abruptly carries worldly accumulation into the graves, paralleling the movement from intense attachment to opened graves in Surah 100.
terra: The rivalry that reached the graves culminates in questioning about blessings, giving the accumulated life of 102:1-2 its account.

luna: The section's bird-crop dictionary image gathers what is taken in; this ayah says a person amasses wealth and counts it, connecting accumulation in the chest with the intense love of wealth in 100:8. | terra: The slanderer gathers wealth and repeatedly counts it, a worldly counterfeit of the final divine gathering and total.
terra: The wealth-gatherer supposes wealth will make him last forever, a false claim of permanence overturned by the section's true final remainder.
terra: The destroyed army becomes like eaten crop-straw, supplying the discarded vegetal residue of the threshing image, though no moral winnowing is stated there.
terra: Woe is directed at worshippers, introducing a judgment in which the outer act alone does not establish inward worth.
terra: Those worshippers are heedless of their prayer, supplying the hidden defect beneath the act named in 107:4.
terra: They perform for display, making the defective interior of 107:5 visible as a concern for outward appearance.
